questions.q: What does this lesson say a Salesforce "cloud" actually is?
options: A completely separate piece of software running on different infrastructure
A packaged product line built on the same underlying Salesforce Platform, not separate software
A storage location for uploaded files only
A term with no real technical meaning
questions.explain: Clouds like Sales Cloud and Service Cloud are product-line bundles of objects, features, and licenses, all built on one shared platform.

questions.q: Which cloud is centered on the case record and built for support teams?
options: Sales Cloud
Commerce Cloud
Service Cloud
Marketing Cloud
questions.explain: Service Cloud gives agents a console for working cases, a knowledge base, and routing tools, as shown in the real console screenshot.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which clouds were grown largely through acquisitions mentioned in Lesson 6?
options: Sales Cloud and Service Cloud, both built entirely in-house
Only Service Cloud, acquired from a third party
Platform, acquired from Microsoft
Marketing Cloud (ExactTarget) and Commerce Cloud (Demandware)
questions.explain: Marketing Cloud grew largely through the ExactTarget acquisition, and Commerce Cloud through the Demandware acquisition.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe "Platform" in relation to the other four clouds?
options: It is simply another name for Sales Cloud
It is a cloud exclusively for e-commerce storefronts
It was discontinued and replaced by Commerce Cloud
It's the underlying foundation every cloud is built on, not a business-function cloud like the others
questions.explain: Platform is the database, security model, and customization tools underneath every cloud — also sellable on its own for fully custom apps.

questions.q: What does the app-branding screenshot in this lesson demonstrate about a cloud like Service Cloud?
options: It cannot be customized in any way
Under the hood, it's configured as a named app with its own branding, switchable from the App Launcher
It only exists as a mobile application, never in a browser
It is identical in every Salesforce organization with no configuration options
questions.explain: The Lightning App Builder screenshot shows the Service Console app's name, description, and App Launcher preview — clouds surface to users as configurable apps.
